 (By Sri. K. Suresh, Advocate)
 :J U D G M E N T:
This is a claim petition U/Sec.166 of MV Act claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest for the injuries suffered by the petitioner in the Motor Vehicle Accident occurred on 05.09.2022.
2.

The averments of the petition in brief is as follows:
On 05.09.2022 at about 2.30 p.m., petitioner was walking on the left side of Banasawadi Main Road near Banasawadi Fire Station to Shree Nidhi Hotel, at that time a Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.22-BH-8760 A, came from Doddabanasawadi towards Subbannapalya with high speed in a rash or negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner from left side.
Due to the said impact the petitioner has sustained fracture of both bones of left leg and other grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident the petitioner was shifted to private clinic and thereafter he was shifted to Bowring and Lady Curzon Hospital at Bengaluru,
wherein he has taken treatment.

entities.text: Bowring and Lady Curzon Hospital at Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The petitioner has spent Rs.50,000/- towards medical and conveyance expenses.
Due to injuries the petitioner has suffered from constant pain and discomforts and he has sustained permanent disability and lost his occupation and earnings.
The accident was occurred due to rash or negligent driving of the Motor vehicle involved in the accident.
Therefore, the respondents being the owner and insurer of the said vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
Hence, this petition.
3. After service of notice, 2nd respondent-Insurance company appeared through it's counsel and filed written statement.
In so far as 1 st respondent- R.C. owner of the offending vehicle is concerned, he remained absent and he has been placed Ex-parte.

4. The written statement averments of the 2nd respondent are hereunder:
The 2nd respondent has admitted the issuance of insurance policy with respect to motor cycle bearing Reg.No.22- BH-8760A and contended that, the liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.

Interalia contended that, the 1st respondent has not complied the mandatory provisions contemplated under 134(c) of M.V.Act by not furnishing the particulars of policy, date, time and place of accident,
Mahantesh G. Goudar vs Hitesh.K on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32214076/
2 particulars of injured and driving licence of the rider.

entities.text: Mahantesh G. Goudar vs Hitesh.K on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, the police have not complied the the mandatory provisions contemplated under 158(6) of M.V.Act by not forwarding all the relevant documents to this respondent.
Further contended that, the rider of the motor cycle was not possessed valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident.
Hence, the respondent No.1 has violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
The insured vehicle had no FC as on the date of alleged accident.
The offending motor cycle was not involved in the accident nor caused injuries to the petitioner.
The petitioner in collusion with the police have created false records against the involvement of the motor cycle to get compensation and lodged the false complaint after lapse of 4 days.
Further, the motor cycle being driven by its rider in a reasonable speed and careful manner and there is no rashness or negligence on the part of rider of motor cycle.
The accident was occurred due to negligence of the petitioner himself, who was crossing the road carelessly without having proper look out of the vehicular movements and it is self fall.
Further, this respondent has denied the injuries sustained by the petitioner.
Likewise treatment taken and amount spent by the petitioner, age, occupation, income and disability sustained by him.
Further contended that, the compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings, the predecessor in the office has framed the following:
:ISSUES:
1.
Whether respondent No.2 proves that, the rider of offended vehicle had no valid and effective D.L. at the time of accident?

2. Whether the petitioner proves that, he met with an accident on 05.09.2022 at about 2.30 p.m., on Banasavadi Main Road, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.22-BH-8760-A and sustained grievous injuries as contended in the petition?
3. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation? If so, how much and from whom?
4. What order or award?
6.
In order to prove the case of the petitioner, he has examined himself as P.W.1 and marked Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.16.
Further, he examined one witness as P.W.2 and marked Ex.P.17 to Ex.P.20. P.W.1 and P.W.2 were cross-examined from the side of respondent No.2.
Respondent No.2 has not adduced any evidence.

Mahantesh G. Goudar vs Hitesh.K on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32214076/
3 7.
Heard the arguments from both side.
Perused the records placed before the Tribunal.

The findings of this Tribunal to the above referred Issues are as under:-
Issue No.1 :- In the Negative.

Issue No.2 :- In the Affirmative Issue No.3 :- In the Partly Affirmative.
 Issue No.4 :- As per the final order  for the following:
 :REASONS:
8. ISSUE No.1:-
According to the 2nd respondent, the rider of motor cycle bearing Reg.No.22-BH-8760 A had no valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident.
However, in order to substantiate the said contentions, the 2 nd respondent has neither adduced oral evidence not produced documentary evidence.

Moreover,
the charge sheet has been filed against the rider of offending vehicle.
Charge sheet submitted by IO does not reveals that rider of offending vehicle was driving the vehicle without valid and effective DL.
Apart from that, the 1st respondent is none other than the rider of offending vehicle.

On perusal of Ex.P.12, it appears to this Tribunal that, the owner/1st respondent of the vehicle has furnished the D.L.
number.
Therefore, it appears to this Tribunal that, the rider of the offending vehicle/1 st respondent was holding valid D.L. to drive the offending vehicle at the time of accident.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the Negative.
9. ISSUE No.2:-
In order to prove this issue, the petitioner has examined himself as P.W.1 by way of filing affidavit in support of his oral examination-in-chief.

Hence,
this Tribunal need not to recapitulate the same once again at this juncture.
In order to prove this issue, P.W.1 has relied on Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.9.
Accordingly, Ex.P.1 is the certified copy FIR pertaining to Cr.No.112/2022.
Ex. P.2
is the certified copy of complaint.
Ex. P.3
is the certified copy of spot mahazar.
Ex . P.4
is the certified copy of spot sketch.
Ex. P.5
is the certified copy of M.V.A. Report.
Ex. P.6
is the certified copy of wound certificate.
Ex. P.7
is the certified copy of charge sheet.
Ex.P.8 is the certified copy of order sheet pertaining to C.C.No.38728/2022.
Ex. P.9
is the certified copy of plea.
10. According to the petitioner, he has sustained injuries in the road accident.
According to respondent No.2, the accident was occurred due to negligence of the petitioner, who was crossing the road carelessly without observing the vehicles movement on the road.
The accident was occurred due to self fall of the petitioner and there was no no negligence on the part of the rider of motor cycle for the occurrence of accident.

Mahantesh G. Goudar vs Hitesh.K on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32214076/
4 11.
To prove the alleged negligence on the part of the petitioner, the Insurance Company has cross-examined the petitioner/P.W.1 in detail.
Nothing has been elicited from mouth of P.W.1 to establish that the accident was took place only on the negligence of petitioner himself.
At the cost of repetition, to substantiate its contention, Insurance company has not placed positive evidence.
Neither the driver of offending vehicle nor ocular witnesses to the incident was examined by 2nd respondent to establish their defence.

12. At this juncture it is worth to refer the decision reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 between Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others,
wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that, "it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied".

13. Further, on careful perusal of Ex.P.1, Ex.P.2 and Ex.P.7, it appears to this Tribunal that, on the basis of complaint, the police have registered the case against the rider of Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.22-BH-8760 A and Investigating officer has submitted Charge sheet as per Ex.P.7 after completing investigation.

A careful perusal of Ex.P.6,
it clearly goes to show that, the injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.
Further, on perusal of Ex.P.7 i.e., final report, it reveals that, the rider of offending vehicle i.e., Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.22-BH-8760 A, arrayed as accused.
Further, on perusal of Ex.P.8 and Ex.P.9 it reveals that, the rider of offending vehicle pleaded guilty before the jurisdictional Magistrate Court.

14. Now, it is worth to rely on the decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka reported in ILR 2003 Karnataka page 493, between Mallamma Vs. Balaju and Others, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held at para 12 as hereunder:
" Filing of the charge sheet against the driver is also a prima-facie case to hold that,
the driver of the said lorry was responsible for the accident and burden shifts on him to prove the same".
15. The other contention of the 2nd respondent is that, there has been 4 days delay in lodging the complaint.
At the cost of repetition, charge sheet has been filed against the rider of the offending vehicle and he has already pleaded guilty in criminal case.

At this juncture, it is worth to refer the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2011 (4) SCC 693, between Ravi Vs. Badrinarayana and Others, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court held at Para 17 and 18 as as hereunder:
"17.
It is well-settled that delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt the claimant's case.

Knowing the Indian conditions as they are, we cannot except a Mahantesh G. Goudar vs Hitesh.K on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32214076/
5
common man to first rush to the Police Station immediately after an accident.
Human nature and family responsibilities occupy the mind of kith and kin to such an extent that they give more importance to get the victim treated rather than to rush to the Police Station.
Under such circumstances, they are not expected to act mechanically with promptitude in lodging the FIR with the Police.
Delay in lodging the FIR thus, cannot be the ground to deny justice to the victim.
18. In cases of delay, the courts are required to examine the evidence with the closer scrutiny and in doing so; the contents of the FIR should also be scrutinized more carefully.

If court finds that there is no indication of fabrication or it has not been concocted or engineered to implicate innocent persons then, even if there is a delay in lodging the FIR, the claim case cannot be dismissed merely on that ground".
16.

The principles reiterated in the above decision are squarely applicable to the facts of the case,
since the respondent No.2 has failed to establish regarding complaint was being lodged colluding with police and more over in the complaint itself the complainant has explained the delay for lodging complaint.
Hence there is no substance in the contention of the 2nd respondent-Insurance company.

17. At the cost of repetition, the contents of complaint and charge sheet clearly reveals that, when the petitioner was walking on the left side of the road, the Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.22-BH-8760 A, came with high speed in a rash or negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner from left side.
The evidence placed on record clearly reveals that the rider of Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.22-BH-8760 A has caused the accident.
Accordingly, Issue No.2 is answered in the Affirmative.
18. ISSUE No.3:-
This issue is with respect to entitlement of relief.
Already this Tribunal has observed that, accident was occurred due to rash or negligent riding of the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.22-BH-8760 A by its rider.
The 2 nd respondent is the insurer and the 1 st respondent is the R.C. owner of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.
Before going to discuss other aspects, it is appropriate to discuss the age and income of the petitioner.
According to the petitioner, he was aged 43 years as on the date of accident.

In order to substantiate the same, the petitioner has produced Ex.P.15, the notarized copy of his Aadhaar Card and the said document discloses that, the date of birth of petitioner is mentioned as 01.01.1979.
The accident was occurred on 05.09.2022.
Hence, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident was 43 years.
Accordingly the age of the petitioner is considered as 43 years.

20. Income:- According to the petitioner, he was working in Cloth Shop and earning a sum of Rs.21,000/- per month as salary and Rs.5,000/- as incentives in total he was earning Rs.26,000/-
per month.
Per-contra, the 2 nd respondent has denied the income of petitioner.
To substantiate his income the petitioner has not produced any documents.
The petitioner has not examined his employer to prove his income.

As such, at this juncture, it is worth to rely on the decision of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka decided in M.F.A. No.101144 of 2020 ( MV-I) on 05.07.2023,
Mahantesh G. Goudar vs Hitesh.K on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32214076/
6 between Ananda Vs. Arun and Another, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka at Para 9 (b)
as hereunder:
" In the absence of any cogent material on record, it is for the courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally.

entities.text: Mahantesh G. Goudar vs Hitesh.K on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: High Court of Karnataka at Para 9 (b)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority for the accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/-.

In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/- per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant".
21. In the absence of any documentary evidence and also non examination of employer the version of petitioner regarding income will not come to his aid.
Hence, this Tribunal will not consider the same.
Per-coontra the notional income of the petitioner is to be considered by relying on the judgment of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka referred to above.

As per the notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority for the accident in the year 2022 is Rs.15,500/-
per month.
It is pertinent to note that, the accident took place on 05.09.2022.
Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.15,500/- per month.

22. Loss of Future Income due to disability:-
In the instant case, the petitioner has averred that, he has sustained fracture of both bones of left leg and other grievous injuries all over the body.
Further, P.W.1 has stated that, he has undergone operation and one rod and three screws were inserted to his left leg.
He has produced wound certificate, and discharge summary, which are marked as Ex.P.6 and Ex.P.10.
On perusal of these documents, it reveal that, the petitioner has sustained above mentioned injuries.
It is relevant to mention that,
respondent

No.2 has disputed the injuries caused to P.W.1.
23
. In order to prove the physical disability/injuries, the petitioner has examined medical witness namely S.A. Somashekara, Orthopedic Surgeon at Bowring and lady Curzon Hospital, Bengaluru as P.W.2.
This witness has filed the affidavit in lieu of his oral examination-in-chief.
In his affidavit he has stated that on 30.05.2023 he has examined the petitioner clinically and radiologically for the assessment of disability.
He also stated that, petitioner has undergone surgery in the form of CRIF with IMIL Nailing on 06.09.2022.

On examination, the petitioner walks with pain and limping,
wasting of left thigh and diffuse swelling of left leg are seen, surgical scars are seen over the left knee and leg.
He also stated that, recent X-ray shows fracture of both bones are united with implants in situ.
Finally P.W.2 has stated that, petitioner has sustained 37% of disability to the left lower limb and 18% to the whole body.
Further deposed that, in view of the disability, it is difficult for the petitioner to work in cloth shop or to do any other manual work or physical work.
P.W.2 has produced 4 documents, which are marked as Ex.P.17 to Ex.P.20.
Ex. P.17
is the OPD record.
Ex. P.18
is the recent X- ray film.
Ex. P.19
is the old X-ray film.
Ex . P.20
is the Case Sheet.
24. P.W.2 was cross-
examined from the side of 2 nd respondent at length.
During the course of cross-examination, he has admitted that, he is not the treated doctor.

He also admitted that, he has Mahantesh G. Goudar vs Hitesh.K on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32214076/
7 not taken opinion from the treated doctor.
Further he has admitted that, fractures are united.
He also admitted that, there is no fracture in knee and ankle of the petitioner.

Further admitted that,
there is no problem in blood circulation.
He also admitted that, he has not assessed the functional disability of the petitioner, but he has assessed the physical disability.

25. On perusal of the discharge summary of petitioner and evidence of medical witness coupled with wound certificate clearly reveals that, petitioner has sustained grievous injury and suffered physical disability.
Further, on careful perusal of the deposition of P.W.2, it is crystal clear that, the fractures are united and P.W.2 has not assessed the functional disability of the petitioner.
Therefore, by considering the avocation of petitioner and injuries, the physical disability assessed by the P.W.2 is on higher side.
Hence, this Tribunal considered the physical disability of the injured as 8% to the whole body.
26. As discussed supra, age of the injured is considered as 43 years and his income is considered as Rs.15,500/- per month.
Annual income comes to Rs.1,86,000/-(15,500 x 12).

Hence, the proper multiplier applicable to the age of injured as per Sarala Verma case is 14.
27.
If we multiplied yearly income with proper multiplier (1,86,000X 14), then it comes to Rs.26,04,000/-.
Already this Tribunal has considered the disability of petitioner as 8% to the whole body.
The same amount of Rs.2,08,320/- is awarded to the Injured/Petitioner under the head of loss of Future Income due to disabiltiy.
28. Medical Expenses:-
In the instant case, the petitioner has stated that, he has incurred Rs.35,000/- towards medical expenses, transportaion and conveyance charges.
In order to substantiate the incurring of medical expenses, the petitioner has produced 9 medical bills as Ex.P.16 for Rs.4,182/-.

After careful perusal of the medical bills, this Tribunal is of the opinion that,
petitioner is entitled for Rs.4,182/- towards medical expenses.
29. Pain and suffering:-
According to the petitioner, his left leg has been operated and inserted one rod and three screws.

Further P.W.1 has stated that, he cannot stand longer period, walk without the help of stick, climb stairs, squat on ground, cannot move his left leg freely, he cannot use Indian type of toilet and he always get pain in his left leg and his left leg has became disabled.

As per medical records and evidence of P.W.2 coupled with Ex.P.10, it appears to this Tribunal that, the petitioner has taken treatment at Bowring and Lady Curzon Hospital, Bengaluru as an inpatient from 05.09.2022 to 13.09.2022 for the period of 9 days.

entities.text: Bowring and Lady Curzon Hospital, Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Further as per the evidence of doctor, it appears to this tribunal that, the petitioner has sustained physical disability.
There is no serious dispute with regard to inpatient for 9 days.
As such, the petitioner has suffered a lot of pain and inconvenience.
Considering all these aspects, the Tribunal grants compensation of Rs.30,000/- under the head of Pain and Sufferings.
30. Loss of income during the laidup period:- The petitioner has produced discharge summary and same has been marked as Ex.P.10.
On perusal of this document, it appears to this Tribunal that, the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient for 9 days.

However, the petitioner has not produced Mahantesh G. Goudar vs Hitesh.K on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32214076/
8 documents to show that, how many days he has taken bed rest.
Naturally it shows that, he might have taken atleast two months rest because of the injuries.
He has averred that, he was working in cloth shop and earning Rs.26,000/- per month.
This Tribunal has already assessed the income of petitioner as Rs.15,500/- per month.
Hence, two months is to be considered as loss of income during laidup period.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.31,000/- as compensation under the head of loss of income during laid up period.
31. Food, Nourishment, Atttendant and Transportation charges:-
In so for as food, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges are concerned, the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatinet for about 9 days i.e., from 05.01.2022 to 13.09.2022.
The petitioner has not produced any documents in this regard.
Further, the petitioner has deposed that, he was discharged with an advise to take follow-up treatment.
As such, he was visiting the Bowring and Lady Curzon Hospital, Bengaluru once in a week for one month and thereafter monthly once.
Further P.W.1 deposed that, for follow-up treatment, he used to travel an Autorickshaw by spending Rs.300/- per trip.
In this regard, the petitioner has not produced any documents.

Hence, looking to the injuries sustained and the period of treatment taken by the petitioner, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.20,000/-
under the head of Food, Nourishment, Atttendant and transportation charges.
32. Loss of future amenities and happiness:- The petitioner was aged about 43 years at the time of accident.
The disability and physical deformity with which the petitioner has to live the rest of his life.
Therefore, he might have suffered pain, discomforts in life and loss of amenities.
By considering the age, nature of injuries, percentage of disabiltiy, Rs.20,000/- is awarded under this head.
33. Future medical expenses:-

The petitioner has stated that, he requires approximately a sumof Rs.50,000/- for the removal of implants and for physiotherapy treatment in private hospital,
Bengaluru.
P.W.2 the medical witness deposed that, the petitioner needs surgery for removal of implant, which would cost around Rs.25,000/- in private set up.
Hence, by considering the future treatment and evidence of P.W.2, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.15,000/- towards future medical expenses.

34. Thus, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
 Heads Amount  1.Towards loss of Future income.

Rs. 2,08,320/-
 2. Towards Medical Expenses.

Rs. 4,182/-
 3. Towards Pain & Suffering.

Rs. 30,000/-
 4. Loss of income during the laidup  period Rs. 31,000/-

5 . Food, Nourishment Atttendant Rs. 20,000/-
 and transportation charges Mahantesh G. Goudar vs Hitesh.K on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32214076/
9  6. Loss of future amenities and Rs. 20,000/-
 happiness.
 7. Towards future medical expenses.
Total.
Hence, petitioner is entitled for just and reasonable amount of Rs.3,28,502/-.
35. Regarding liability and interest.
Driving License:- Driving License:-
Already this Tribunal has answered issue No.1 in this regard.
Insurance Policy and liability:-
In the instant case, respondent No.2 has admitted the issuance of insurance policy with respect to motor cycle bearing Reg.No.22-BH-8760 A.
Hence, the respondent No.2 shall pay compensation amount to the petitioner.
36. In view of the decision reported in MFA NO: 30131- 2019 dtd, 12.5.2020 rate of interest on the compensation amount is awarded at 6% p.a. from the date of petition.
Accordingly, Issue No.2 is answered in the Partly Affirmative.
37. ISSUE No.3:-
In view of discussions made above, I proceed to pass the following.

:ORDER:
Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with costs of the petition.
Petitioner is awarded just and reasonable compensation of Rs.3,28,502/- (Rupees Three Lakhs Twenty Eight Thousand Five Hundred and Two only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition to till the date of depositing of the compensation amount in the Tribunal.
Respondent No.2 shall deposit the compensation in the Tribunal within 2 months from the date of this judgment.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw Award Accordingly.

1  (Insurer of Motor Cycle-bearing  Reg.No.22-BH-8760 A  Policy No.201250020121704936000000  Valid: 26.03.2022 to 25.03.2027)
 (By Sri. K. Suresh, Advocate)
 :J U D G M E N T:
This is a claim petition U/Sec.166 of MV Act claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest for the injuries suffered by the petitioner in the Motor Vehicle Accident occurred on 05.09.2022.
2.
opennyai_summary.facts:
Due to injuries the petitioner has suffered from constant pain and discomforts and he has sustained permanent disability and lost his occupation and earnings.
The accident was occurred due to rash or negligent driving of the Motor vehicle involved in the accident.
Therefore, the respondents being the owner and insurer of the said vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
Hence, the respondent No.1 has violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
The insured vehicle had no FC as on the date of alleged accident.
The offending motor cycle was not involved in the accident nor caused injuries to the petitioner.
The petitioner in collusion with the police have created false records against the involvement of the motor cycle to get compensation and lodged the false complaint after lapse of 4 days.
Further, the motor cycle being driven by its rider in a reasonable speed and careful manner and there is no rashness or negligence on the part of rider of motor cycle.
The accident was occurred due to negligence of the petitioner himself, who was crossing the road carelessly without having proper look out of the vehicular movements and it is self fall.
Likewise treatment taken and amount spent by the petitioner, age, occupation, income and disability sustained by him.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
Further contended that, the rider of the motor cycle was not possessed valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident.
Further contended that, the compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive and exorbitant.
opennyai_summary.issue:
5. On the basis of the above pleadings, the predecessor in the office has framed the following:
:ISSUES:
1.
Whether respondent No.2 proves that, the rider of offended vehicle had no valid and effective D.L. at the time of accident?
2. Whether the petitioner proves that, he met with an accident on 05.09.2022 at about 2.30 p.m., on Banasavadi Main Road, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.22-BH-8760-A and sustained grievous injuries as contended in the petition?
3. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation? If so, how much and from whom?
4. What order or award?
6.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The accident was occurred due to self fall of the petitioner and there was no no negligence on the part of the rider of motor cycle for the occurrence of accident.
Nothing has been elicited from mouth of P.W.1 to establish that the accident was took place only on the negligence of petitioner himself.
At the cost of repetition, to substantiate its contention, Insurance company has not placed positive evidence.
Neither the driver of offending vehicle nor ocular witnesses to the incident was examined by 2nd respondent to establish their defence.
12. At this juncture it is worth to refer the decision reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 between Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others,
wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that, "it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
A careful perusal of Ex.P.6,
it clearly goes to show that, the injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.
Further, on perusal of Ex.P.7 i.e., final report, it reveals that, the rider of offending vehicle i.e., Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.22-BH-8760 A, arrayed as accused.
Further, on perusal of Ex.P.8 and Ex.P.9 it reveals that, the rider of offending vehicle pleaded guilty before the jurisdictional Magistrate Court.
The principles reiterated in the above decision are squarely applicable to the facts of the case,
since the respondent No.2 has failed to establish regarding complaint was being lodged colluding with police and more over in the complaint itself the complainant has explained the delay for lodging complaint.
Hence there is no substance in the contention of the 2nd respondent-Insurance company.
17. At the cost of repetition, the contents of complaint and charge sheet clearly reveals that, when the petitioner was walking on the left side of the road, the Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.22-BH-8760 A, came with high speed in a rash or negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner from left side.
The evidence placed on record clearly reveals that the rider of Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.22-BH-8760 A has caused the accident.
Already this Tribunal has observed that, accident was occurred due to rash or negligent riding of the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.22-BH-8760 A by its rider.
The 2 nd respondent is the insurer and the 1 st respondent is the R.C. owner of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.
Hence, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident was 43 years.
The petitioner has not examined his employer to prove his income.
The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority for the accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/-.
In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/- per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant".
21. In the absence of any documentary evidence and also non examination of employer the version of petitioner regarding income will not come to his aid.
Therefore, by considering the avocation of petitioner and injuries, the physical disability assessed by the P.W.2 is on higher side.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Per-coontra the notional income of the petitioner is to be considered by relying on the judgment of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka referred to above.
By considering the age, nature of injuries, percentage of disabiltiy, Rs.20,000/- is awarded under this head.
33. Future medical expenses:-
Hence, by considering the future treatment and evidence of P.W.2, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.15,000/- towards future medical expenses.
34. Thus, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
 Heads Amount  1.Towards loss of Future income.
Rs. 2,08,320/-
 2. Towards Medical Expenses.
Rs. 30,000/-
 4. Loss of income during the laidup  period Rs. 31,000/-
Rs. 15,000/-
Hence, petitioner is entitled for just and reasonable amount of Rs.3,28,502/-.
Insurance Policy and liability:-
In the instant case, respondent No.2 has admitted the issuance of insurance policy with respect to motor cycle bearing Reg.No.22-BH-8760 A.
Hence, the respondent No.2 shall pay compensation amount to the petitioner.
36. In view of the decision reported in MFA NO: 30131- 2019 dtd, 12.5.2020 rate of interest on the compensation amount is awarded at 6% p.a. from the date of petition.
Accordingly, Issue No.2 is answered in the Partly Affirmative.
In view of discussions made above, I proceed to pass the following.
:ORDER:
Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with costs of the petition.
Petitioner is awarded just and reasonable compensation of Rs.3,28,502/- (Rupees Three Lakhs Twenty Eight Thousand Five Hundred and Two only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition to till the date of depositing of the compensation amount in the Tribunal.
Respondent No.2 shall deposit the compensation in the Tribunal within 2 months from the date of this judgment.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw Award Accordingly.

On deposit of compensation amount, office to pay 80% of amount with interest through E- Mahantesh G. Goudar vs Hitesh.K on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32214076/
10 payment to the petitioner, after due identification as per rules and after verifying the stay order from the Hon'ble Appellate Court and remaining 20% with interest shall be invested in F.D. in his name in any nationalized bank for a period of 3 years.
It is clarified that, the petitioner is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on the deposit amount from time to time.
